title: Generating text, images and audio
hook: Language, image, speech and multimodal generators, and what must stay human-checked.
inPlainWords: Generative models create new content that looks like what they were trained on. That is powerful, and it also means they can create convincing errors.

useCase.title: Write 500 product descriptions and add lifestyle images
useCase.story: A new catalog has 500 products. Each needs a description and one clean background image. The specs come from a supplier spreadsheet.

approaches.name: Language model for text
approaches.what: Draft descriptions from the spec sheet.
approaches.avoidWhen: Facts must be exact and no one checks them.
approaches.example: Turn "steel, 1.2 liters, 220 volts" into a friendly description.

approaches.name: Image generation
approaches.what: Create images from descriptions, or edit existing ones.
approaches.greatWhen: Backgrounds, mood images and concept art.
approaches.avoidWhen: Showing the exact product with correct details.
approaches.example: Place a real product photo on a kitchen scene.

approaches.name: Speech and audio
approaches.what: Turn text into natural voice, or voice into text.

approaches.name: Multimodal models
approaches.what: One model reads and writes text, images and sound.

approaches.name: Synthetic data
approaches.what: Generate fake but realistic examples for testing or training.
approaches.avoidWhen: As your only training data. Errors get baked in.
approaches.example: Make 1,000 fake complaint emails to test the bot.

approaches.name: Grounding and human review
approaches.what: Feed in the real spec sheet, and have a person check the facts and the brand.

challenge.question: Generated descriptions might invent specs. What is the best setup?

options.why: Invented specs lead to returns and complaints.

options.text: Draft only from the spec sheet, check numbers automatically, and review a sample and all flagged items
options.why: It keeps the model tied to real facts and catches mistakes before customers do.

options.text: Ask the model to recall the specs from memory
Draft from the spec sheet, but publish with no review
options.why: Faster and mostly right, but errors slip through.

bestCase.title: Ground it in real specs, check automatically, review a sample
bestCase.example: The model drafts from the spec sheet only. A script compares numbers in the text with the sheet. An editor reviews a sample and all flagged items. Product photos get generated backgrounds, but the product itself is always the real photo.

worstCase.title: Publishing unchecked output
worstCase.example: A blender description claims "2,000-watt motor, dishwasher safe" because the model liked the phrase. The spec sheet says 800 watts, hand wash. Returns and complaints follow, and the brand looks careless.

route.travelling: Spec row: steel kettle, 1.2 liters, 220 volts

steps.label: Draft with the model
steps.goes: It writes a description using only those specs.

steps.label: Automatic fact check
steps.goes: Every number in the text matches the sheet.
steps.goesWrong: There is no check, so an invented "2,000-watt, dishwasher safe" claim sails through.

steps.label: Image step
steps.goes: The real product photo is placed on a generated kitchen scene.

steps.label: Human review
steps.goes: An editor reviews flagged items and a sample.

takeaway: Generated content needs grounding, checking, and a person in the loop wherever facts matter.
